accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes the institutional basis of NITI Aayog?
o: It was created by an Act of Parliament
It was created by a constitutional amendment
It was created by a Presidential Ordinance
It was created by a Union Cabinet resolution
accepted.x: NITI Aayog is a non-constitutional and non-statutory body created by a Union Cabinet resolution.
accepted.tq: Identify the exact legal instrument instead of assuming that a national institution must be statutory.
accepted.sec: Legal status of NITI Aayog - instrument, federalism approach, think tank  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the composition of NITI Aayog:
1. The Prime Minister is its Chairperson.
2. Its Vice-Chairperson is appointed by the Prime Minister.
3. The resolution fixes the number of full-time members at five.
4. Up to two part-time members may be drawn from universities and research institutions.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The Prime Minister is the Chairperson, appoints the Vice-Chairperson, and may nominate up to two part-time members from universities and research bodies. The resolution does not prescribe a fixed number of full-time members.
accepted.tq: Test the fixed-number trap by separating provisions that are flexible from those expressly specified.
accepted.sec: NITI Aayog - year, body replaced, composition, Vice-Chairman  [APPSC]

accepted.s: With reference to NITI Aayog, which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: Ex officio members — Up to four Union Ministers nominated by the Prime Minister
Part-time members — Permanent representatives of all State Governments
Chief Executive Officer — Elected by the Governing Council
Special invitees — Nominated by the Vice-Chairperson alone
accepted.x: NITI Aayog may have up to four ex officio Union Ministers nominated by the Prime Minister. Its CEO is appointed by the Prime Minister, and special invitees are also nominated by the Prime Minister.
accepted.tq: Match each component with the authority responsible for its inclusion or appointment.
accepted.sec: NITI Aayog - year, body replaced, composition, Vice-Chairman  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Ashok Kumar Lahiri assumed the office of Vice-Chairperson of NITI Aayog on which date?
accepted.x: Ashok Kumar Lahiri, formerly Chief Economic Adviser, was appointed Vice-Chairperson of NITI Aayog on 25 April 2026.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the appointment date from the dates of NITI Aayog’s formation and Governing Council meetings.
accepted.sec: NITI Aayog - year, body replaced, composition, Vice-Chairman  [APPSC]

accepted.s: In the planning process followed by the Planning Commission, plans were placed before which sequence of institutions?
accepted.x: Plans prepared through the Planning Commission went to the National Development Council, then the Cabinet and thereafter Parliament.
accepted.tq: Use the institutional sequence and eliminate bodies not involved in plan approval.
accepted.sec: Planning Commission - year, resolution, chairman, dissolution and PM who abolished it  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
A. Announcement of the abolition of the Planning Commission
B. Formation of NITI Aayog
C. Establishment of the Planning Commission
D. Appointment of Ashok Kumar Lahiri as Vice-Chairperson of NITI Aayog
accepted.x: The Planning Commission was established in March 1950, its abolition was announced on 15 August 2014, NITI Aayog came into existence on 1 January 2015, and Ashok Kumar Lahiri was appointed on 25 April 2026.
accepted.tq: Fix the earliest and latest events first, then place the 2014 and 2015 events between them.
accepted.sec: Planning Commission - year, resolution, chairman, dissolution and PM who abolished it  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The abolition of the Planning Commission was announced by which Prime Minister on 15 August 2014?
accepted.x: Prime Minister Narendra Modi announced the abolition of the Planning Commission on 15 August 2014; it was replaced by NITI Aayog on 1 January 2015.
accepted.tq: Apply the wrong-person-for-the-deed trap to distinguish the announcing Prime Minister from earlier Prime Ministers.
accepted.sec: Planning Commission - year, resolution, chairman, dissolution and PM who abolished it  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which approach is most closely associated with the federalism model of NITI Aayog?
o: Judicial federalism controlled by the Supreme Court
Centralised federalism based exclusively on Union directives
Fiscal federalism limited to tax devolution
Cooperative federalism with a bottom-up approach
accepted.x: NITI Aayog promotes cooperative federalism and follows a bottom-up approach. Its State rankings also provide an element of competitive federalism.
accepted.tq: Separate the principal approach from related but narrower forms of federalism.
accepted.sec: Legal status of NITI Aayog - instrument, federalism approach, think tank  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT a stated area of the mandate of NITI Aayog?
o: Conducting constitutional litigation for State Governments
accepted.x: The four stated areas are knowledge and innovation, NITI for States, transformational change, and monitoring and evaluation. Constitutional litigation is not included among them.
accepted.tq: Find the option that does not belong to the official functional group.
accepted.sec: Legal status of NITI Aayog - instrument, federalism approach, think tank  [APPSC]

accepted.s: NITI Aayog is described as the government’s think tank and policy dynamo primarily because it performs which role?
o: It replaces Parliament in making laws
It directly collects all taxes for the Union
It provides policy advice, promotes innovation and supports transformational change
It exercises judicial review over State policies
accepted.x: NITI Aayog functions as a policy think tank by providing policy inputs, promoting knowledge and innovation, supporting States and pursuing transformational change.
accepted.tq: Infer the institution’s practical role from its advisory and policy-development functions.
accepted.sec: Legal status of NITI Aayog - instrument, federalism approach, think tank  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which body of NITI Aayog tracks the performance of Union ministries?
accepted.x: The Development Monitoring and Evaluation Office, or DMEO, tracks the performance of ministries.
accepted.tq: Match the monitoring function with the specialised evaluation office rather than with a federal-engagement hub.
accepted.sec: Legal status of NITI Aayog - instrument, federalism approach, think tank  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the Governing Council of NITI Aayog:
1. It includes the Prime Minister.
2. It includes the Chief Ministers of all States.
3. It includes the Lieutenant Governors of Union Territories without legislatures.
4. It includes only elected representatives and excludes special invitees.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The Governing Council includes the Prime Minister, Chief Ministers of all States, Chief Ministers of Union Territories with legislatures, Lieutenant Governors of other Union Territories, ex officio members, the Vice-Chairperson, full-time members and special invitees. Statement 4 is false.
accepted.tq: Test composition by identifying the excluded category hidden behind the word ‘only’.
accepted.sec: NITI bodies and hubs - Governing Council, Regional Councils, hubs → function  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Chief Ministers of which Union Territories are members of the Governing Council of NITI Aayog?
o: Puducherry, Lakshadweep, and Andaman and Nicobar Islands
Delhi, Jammu and Kashmir, and Puducherry
Delhi, Chandigarh, and Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu
accepted.x: The Governing Council includes the Chief Ministers of Union Territories having legislatures: Delhi, Jammu and Kashmir, and Puducherry.
accepted.tq: Use the legislature-based classification to distinguish Union Territories represented by Chief Ministers.
accepted.sec: NITI bodies and hubs - Governing Council, Regional Councils, hubs → function  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Regional Councils of NITI Aayog are primarily constituted for:
o: Permanent supervision of every State’s finances
Specific regional issues for a fixed period
accepted.x: Regional Councils are formed to address specific regional issues and operate for a fixed period. They are chaired by the Prime Minister or his nominee and include the Chief Ministers and Lieutenant Governors of the region.
accepted.tq: Identify the temporary, issue-specific body rather than attributing permanent constitutional functions to it.
accepted.sec: NITI bodies and hubs - Governing Council, Regional Councils, hubs → function  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Who may chair a Regional Council constituted by NITI Aayog?
o: The Chief Minister of the largest State in the region
The Prime Minister or his nominee
accepted.x: A Regional Council is chaired by the Prime Minister or his nominee; Chief Ministers and Lieutenant Governors of the concerned region are included in it.
accepted.tq: Apply the authority-power test to identify who can chair the body.
accepted.sec: NITI bodies and hubs - Governing Council, Regional Councils, hubs → function  [APPSC]

accepted.s: SETUs, supported by NITI Aayog under the State Support Mission, are intended to help States prepare:
accepted.x: NITI Aayog assists States in setting up State Economic and Transformation Units, or SETUs, to prepare State Vision@2047 plans.
accepted.tq: Expand the acronym and link the institutional support to its stated planning output.
accepted.sec: NITI bodies and hubs - Governing Council, Regional Councils, hubs → function  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The SDG India Index primarily measures:
o: States’ progress towards Sustainable Development Goals
Multidimensional poverty through only health indicators
accepted.x: The SDG India Index assesses the progress of States and Union Territories towards the Sustainable Development Goals.
accepted.tq: Match the index with its subject rather than with another NITI Aayog index.
accepted.sec: NITI indices and reports → subject  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The fourth edition of the SDG India Index, released in July 2024, used how many indicators?
accepted.x: The fourth edition of the SDG India Index for 2023–24 used 113 indicators.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the exact indicator count from nearby rounded numerical distractors.
accepted.sec: NITI indices and reports → subject  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Andhra Pradesh’s score in the SDG India Index 2023–24 was 74, placing it in which category?
accepted.x: Andhra Pradesh scored 74 in the SDG India Index 2023–24 and was categorised as a Front Runner.
accepted.tq: Use the score-category association and avoid confusing it with the Aspirational Districts classification.
accepted.sec: NITI indices and reports → subject  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: India Electric Mobility Index — Agricultural poverty
Export Preparedness Index — States’ export readiness
School Education Quality Index — Export competitiveness
accepted.x: The Export Preparedness Index assesses States’ export readiness. The GROW report concerns wasteland restoration through agroforestry, while the other two indices have education and electric mobility subjects respectively.
accepted.tq: Use subject-based matching to detect the swapped purposes of neighbouring indices.
accepted.sec: NITI indices and reports → subject  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Export Preparedness Index:
1. Its first edition was released in 2020.
2. Andhra Pradesh ranked fifth among large States in the 2024 edition.
3. Andhra Pradesh had ranked eighth in the 2022 edition.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct: the first edition was released in 2020, Andhra Pradesh ranked eighth in 2022 and fifth among large States in the 2024 edition.
accepted.tq: Track the change in rank across editions while checking the dates separately.
accepted.sec: NITI indices and reports → subject  [APPSC]

accepted.s: What does the acronym GROW in the NITI Aayog report refer to?
o: Greening and Restoration of Wasteland with Agroforestry
Growth and Resource Optimisation for Water
accepted.x: GROW stands for Greening and Restoration of Wasteland with Agroforestry.
accepted.tq: Test the exact expansion of the acronym, not a broad environmental interpretation.
accepted.sec: NITI indices and reports → subject  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes the India Electric Mobility Index mentioned in relation to NITI Aayog?
o: It measures only export readiness using 113 indicators.
It measures e-mobility across States and its second edition used 16 indicators.
It ranks schools using indicators supplied by the former MHRD.
It measures multidimensional poverty using 12 indicators.
accepted.x: The India Electric Mobility Index assesses e-mobility across States. Its second edition, released in September 2026 with WRI India, used 16 indicators with weights of 50/30/20.
accepted.tq: Separate the subject and indicator count of this index from those of the SDG and MPI reports.
accepted.sec: NITI indices and reports → subject  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The School Education Quality Index was prepared by NITI Aayog in association with:
o: The then Ministry of Human Resource Development
accepted.x: The School Education Quality Index was prepared with the then Ministry of Human Resource Development.
accepted.tq: Use the institution–partner association and distinguish it from the partners of other NITI indices.
accepted.sec: NITI indices and reports → subject  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which institution is the nodal agency for poverty estimation in India in the context of the material under consideration?
o: NITI Aayog, earlier the Planning Commission
The Goods and Services Tax Council
accepted.x: NITI Aayog, which succeeded the Planning Commission, is the nodal agency for poverty estimation.
accepted.tq: Identify the institutional continuity despite the change from Planning Commission to NITI Aayog.
accepted.sec: NITI indices and reports → subject  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the Global MPI from the National MPI of India?
o: Global MPI uses 10 indicators, while National MPI uses 12 indicators, adding maternal health and bank account.
Global MPI has 12 indicators, while National MPI has 10 indicators.
National MPI measures only income poverty, unlike the Global MPI.
Both use exactly the same 10 indicators.
accepted.x: The Global MPI developed by UNDP and OPHI uses 10 indicators. India’s National MPI uses 12 indicators by adding maternal health and bank account dimensions.
accepted.tq: Compare the indicator counts first, then identify the two additional National MPI indicators.
accepted.sec: National MPI vs Global MPI - indicators, AP figures  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Global Multidimensional Poverty Index is associated with which institutions?
o: NITI Aayog and the Finance Commission
accepted.x: The Global MPI is associated with the United Nations Development Programme and the Oxford Poverty and Human Development Initiative.
accepted.tq: Apply the report–institution matching method to distinguish global and national producers.
accepted.sec: National MPI vs Global MPI - indicators, AP figures  [APPSC]

accepted.s: India’s multidimensional poverty ratio declined from 29.17% in 2013–14 to which level in 2022–23?
accepted.x: India’s multidimensional poverty ratio fell from 29.17% in 2013–14 to 11.28% in 2022–23.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the national time-series figure from Andhra Pradesh’s headcount and the earlier national poverty estimate.
accepted.sec: National MPI vs Global MPI - indicators, AP figures  [APPSC]

accepted.s: According to the NITI Aayog discussion paper cited, how many people escaped multidimensional poverty in India during the relevant period?
accepted.x: The NITI Aayog discussion paper reported that 24.82 crore people escaped multidimensional poverty.
accepted.tq: Keep the absolute number separate from the percentage figures used in the same poverty assessment.
accepted.sec: National MPI vs Global MPI - indicators, AP figures  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Global MPI value for India in 2025 was:
accepted.x: India’s Global MPI value was 0.061 in 2025, compared with 0.064 in 2024.
accepted.tq: Separate the Global MPI value from the National MPI value and the earlier Andhra Pradesh value.
accepted.sec: National MPI vs Global MPI - indicators, AP figures  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Match the following NITI MPI indicators for Andhra Pradesh with their values:
A. Headcount ratio
B. Intensity
C. MPI
D. Rural HCR

1. 41.12%
2. 6.06%
3. 0.025
4. 7.71%

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: For Andhra Pradesh, the headcount ratio was 6.06%, intensity was 41.12%, MPI was 0.025 and rural headcount ratio was 7.71%.
accepted.tq: Start with the distinctive MPI decimal and then match the percentage indicators.
accepted.sec: National MPI vs Global MPI - indicators, AP figures  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following statements correctly compares Andhra Pradesh and India in the NITI MPI 2023 table for 2019–21?
o: AP had a higher headcount ratio and higher intensity than India.
AP had a lower headcount ratio and lower intensity than India.
AP had a higher headcount ratio but lower intensity than India.
AP had the same MPI as India.
accepted.x: Andhra Pradesh had a headcount ratio of 6.06% and intensity of 41.12%, both lower than India’s 14.96% and 44.39%. Its MPI was 0.025 compared with India’s 0.066.
accepted.tq: Compare each column separately instead of relying on the overall direction of only one indicator.
accepted.sec: National MPI vs Global MPI - indicators, AP figures  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The rural and urban headcount ratios for Andhra Pradesh in the NITI MPI table were respectively:
accepted.x: Andhra Pradesh recorded a rural headcount ratio of 7.71% and an urban headcount ratio of 2.20%. The figures 19.28% and 5.27% relate to India.
accepted.tq: Read the rural–urban pair together and avoid swapping the State and national columns.
accepted.sec: National MPI vs Global MPI - indicators, AP figures  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Andhra Pradesh’s MPI declined from 0.053 in 2015–16 to which value in the NITI MPI 2023 table?
accepted.x: Andhra Pradesh’s MPI declined from 0.053 in 2015–16 to 0.025 in the NITI MPI 2023 table.
accepted.tq: Trace the State’s change over time and distinguish it from Kerala’s and India’s reported values.
accepted.sec: National MPI vs Global MPI - indicators, AP figures  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the ranking and comparative position of Andhra Pradesh in MPI?
o: AP ranked second; Kerala and Bihar had identical MPI values.
AP ranked first; Bihar had the lowest MPI and Kerala the highest.
AP ranked ninth; Kerala had the highest MPI and Bihar the lowest.
AP ranked ninth; Kerala had the lowest MPI and Bihar the highest among the cited States.
accepted.x: Andhra Pradesh ranked ninth by MPI. Kerala recorded the best cited value of 0.002, while Bihar recorded the worst cited value of 0.16.
accepted.tq: Use the ranking together with the best–worst comparison to reject reversed positions.
accepted.sec: National MPI vs Global MPI - indicators, AP figures  [APPSC]

accepted.s: According to the Planning Commission’s 2011–12 estimate, Andhra Pradesh’s poverty ratio was compared with the national ratio as follows:
accepted.x: The Planning Commission estimated poverty in Andhra Pradesh at 9.20% in 2011–12, compared with 21.92% for India as a whole.
accepted.tq: Check both the State and national figures together to catch a reversed comparison.
accepted.sec: National MPI vs Global MPI - indicators, AP figures  [APPSC]
